The part that comes next

Publishing the book is a milestone. It is not the end of the journey.

You have put time, imagination and care into creating a book. The next challenge is helping the right people find it, understand what makes it worth reading and remember you when they are ready for another story.

That takes more than posting a cover or hoping the right person finds your product page. It takes a thoughtful path from discovery to connection.

The bigger picture

From being discovered to being remembered.

Where I can support you

Different authors need different things. The right starting point depends on where you are.

You do not need every service. We can look at what you have already built, what you want to achieve and what would make the biggest difference next.

01

Book discovery & visibility

Find better ways to put your books in front of relevant families, parents, educators and reading communities, including opportunities beyond Amazon.

02

Book pages & presentation

Make it easier for visitors to understand your book, its audience and why it may be a good fit for their family or classroom.

03

Author websites

Create an online home where people can meet you, explore your books, find useful resources and discover what to read next.

04

Audience & reader connections

Build thoughtful ways for interested readers to stay connected with your work instead of relying on a single platform to reach them.

05

Reader journeys & retention

Think about what happens after the first purchase and create natural next steps that help readers explore more of your books.

06

Launches & seasonal visibility

Plan relevant ways to introduce new books or bring existing titles into seasonal conversations and reading moments.

A useful recommendation starts with your actual book and your current situation. I will not assume what is missing before taking a proper look.

A place for readers to discover more of your world.
Beyond the marketplace

Your book can be sold somewhere else. Your author home should belong to you.

Amazon and social platforms can play an important role in helping people find your books. But an author website gives you a place of your own to introduce your work, share useful resources and make it easier for readers to find you again.

  • A clear home for your books and author story
  • Individual pages that help readers explore each title
  • Useful resources for parents, families and educators
  • A way for interested readers to choose to stay connected
  • A place to introduce future books and related work
Talk about your author website ↗
A better question

What happens after someone discovers your book?

One good reading experience can be the beginning of a relationship.

A family may enjoy one story and want to find another. A teacher may want to revisit your resources. A parent may want to hear about your next release. The opportunity is to make those next steps clear and useful, without overwhelming readers with constant promotion.

Stay useful. Stay human. Give readers a reason to remember you.

A note from Joshua

Hi, I am Joshua.

I work with children's book authors who want more families to discover their books and more readers to stay connected with their work.

I believe a book deserves more than a product listing and a few promotional posts. It deserves a thoughtful path to the people who will appreciate it, and a way for those readers to discover more from the author.

Through The Echoes, I look at the bigger picture: how people find your books, what they understand when they arrive, and what gives them a reason to return.

Start a conversation ↗
A few useful answers

Questions authors often ask.

You do not need to have everything figured out before we talk.

Do you only work with children's book authors?

Children's books are the main focus of The Echoes. The work is especially suited to independent and self-published children's authors, including those writing picture books, early readers, fiction and educational titles.

Do you only help authors who sell on Amazon?

No. Amazon may be one part of an author's sales journey, but discovery and reader relationships can happen in many other places too. The right channels depend on the book and its audience.

What if I do not know exactly what I need?

That is completely fine. Tell me about your book, what you have tried so far and what you would like to improve. We can work out a sensible place to begin.

Do you offer paid professional support?

Yes. The support is shaped around the work involved and your goals. If we decide there is a good fit, I will explain what the work includes and the cost before anything begins.

Can you review my book or website first?

Yes. Share the relevant book or website link when you get in touch. I can look at the information available and discuss the opportunities that are most relevant to your situation.
